title: tbl.now — AI Agent Skill Guide
text: tbl.now provides tbl_now S3 class: tibble extension epidemiological nowcasting carries two time indices — event_date (something happened) report_date (recorded) — plus modelling metadata (strata, covariates, temporal effects, now, units, data type). fully dplyr-compatible. tbl.now data-structure + specification layer, modelling engine. standardises/validates data stores lazy specs; actual nowcasting done downstream diseasenowcasting. Every tbl_now auto-computes three protected numeric columns: Removing protected column downgrades object back plain tibble (warning). Protected columns also include event_date, report_date, case_count (count types).
code: library(tbl.now) library(dplyr)

title: tbl.now — AI Agent Skill Guide
text: event_date/report_date accept tidy-select (bare names strings). Units data type inferred default ("auto"). Useful arguments: now = — “-” date nowcast. Defaults max(report_date). event_units / report_units — "days" | "weeks" | "months" | "years" | "numeric"; "auto" infers spacing. report_units must coarser equal event_units. align_weeks = TRUE — weekly data, snaps dates .delay integer (see ). may pass .delay + one date instead dates; missing date reconstructed. Always check worked:
code: # Linelist — one row per observed case (no counts column) tn <- tbl_now(   denguedat,   event_date  = onset_week,      # or "onset_week"   report_date = report_week,   strata      = gender,   verbose     = FALSE )  # Count data — one row per (event, report[, strata]) with a counts column tn <- tbl_now(   mpoxdat,   event_date  = dx_date,   report_date = dx_report_date,   case_count  = n,               # REQUIRED for count data types   strata      = race,   data_type   = "count-incidence",   verbose     = FALSE ) is_tbl_now(tn)            # TRUE validate_tbl_now(tn)      # errors if invalid tn                        # print() shows the footer with all attributes

title: tbl.now — AI Agent Skill Guide
text: Three data types: find , build data_type = "auto" read back: inference heuristic (infer_data_type): case_count column → "linelist". decrease → "count-incidence" (incremental counts go ); monotonically non-decreasing → "count-cumulative". auto guess wrong (e.g. genuinely cumulative data happens never decrease small sample), pass data_type = explicitly.

what: Skill: mark whether data is right-censored
title: tbl.now — AI Agent Skill Guide
text: is_censored flags reports arrive artificial batches representing right-censoring rather true reporting dynamics (e.g. lab outage week reports land later day). is_censored attribute stores name logical column (TRUE/FALSE per row). tell whether dataset censored: .null(get_is_censored(tn)) → TRUE means censoring indicator set. censoring column must logical validate_tbl_now() rejects .
code: df <- df |> mutate(was_batched = report_date == as.Date("2021-03-15")) tn <- tbl_now(df, event_date = onset, report_date = reported,               is_censored = was_batched, verbose = FALSE)  # or after creation: tn <- add_is_censored(tn, was_batched)     # errors if one is already set tn <- change_is_censored(tn, was_batched)  # replace (pass NULL to clear) tn <- remove_is_censored(tn)  get_is_censored(tn)   # column name, or NULL if not censored

title: tbl.now — AI Agent Skill Guide
text: Temporal effects (calendar covariates Fourier seasonality) stored lazily spec, materialised columns demand. add_temporal_effects() can called repeatedly (appends specs); can mix date_type = "event_date" "report_date". Seasonality / Fourier: seasons cycle periods. daily data weekly seasonality use seasons = 52, season_length = 7 (period = 364 days); season_length defaults 1 (period = seasons). Replace clear: Order matters: compute_temporal_effects() add_temporal_effects() -op. replace_temporal_effects() removes computed columns — call compute_temporal_effects() afterward.
code: # 1) build a spec spec <- temporal_effects(   day_of_week   = FALSE,   weekend       = FALSE,   day_of_month  = FALSE,   month_of_year = TRUE,   week_of_year  = TRUE,   seasons       = integer(0),   # Fourier periods, e.g. c(7, 52, 365)   season_length = 1,            # multiply each season; period = seasons * season_length   holidays      = NULL          # an almanac::rcalendar(), see next skill )  # 2) attach (NO columns created yet). date_type = "event_date" (default) or "report_date" tn <- add_temporal_effects(tn, spec, date_type = "event_date")  # 3) materialise the columns when ready for modelling tn <- compute_temporal_effects(tn, overwrite = FALSE)  get_temporal_effects(tn)       # list of specs (length 0 = none attached) get_temporal_effect_cols(tn)   # character(0) before compute; column names after tn <- replace_temporal_effects(tn, temporal_effects(week_of_year = TRUE))  # drops old computed cols tn <- remove_temporal_effects(tn)                                          # clears spec + cols

what: Skill: calendar effects for ANY country (custom almanac holidays)
title: tbl.now — AI Agent Skill Guide
text: Holidays use almanac package (v1.0). temporal_effects(holidays = ...) accepts almanac_rcalendar. restrict almanac::cal_us_federal() — build calendar recurring rules rholiday(rschedule, name) rcalendar(). Building blocks: yearly(), monthly(), weekly() recurrence rules refined recur_on_day_of_month(), recur_on_month_of_year(), recur_on_day_of_week(), etc.; wrap rule rholiday(); combine rcalendar(). almanac Suggests — install missing.
code: library(almanac)  # A fixed-date holiday: Mexican Independence Day, every Sep 16 indep <- yearly() |>   recur_on_month_of_year("Sep") |>   recur_on_day_of_month(16)  # Combine custom + built-in holidays into one calendar mx_calendar <- rcalendar(   rholiday(indep, "Mexican Independence Day"),   hol_new_years_day(),   hol_christmas() )  # Sanity-check which dates are holidays almanac::alma_in(as.Date(c("2023-09-16", "2023-12-25", "2023-06-01")), mx_calendar) #> TRUE TRUE FALSE  # Use it as a temporal effect tn <- tn |>   add_temporal_effects(temporal_effects(holidays = mx_calendar)) |>   compute_temporal_effects()

what: Skill: which dplyr verbs to use (and which to avoid)
title: tbl.now — AI Agent Skill Guide
text: tbl_now implements dplyr generics attributes survive data manipulation: Rules thumb: ✅ Use filter, select, mutate, arrange, group_by/ungroup, rename freely — temporal-effects spec attributes preserved dplyr never triggers temporal-effect computation. ⚠️ remove protected columns (.event_num, .report_num, .delay, event_date, report_date, case_count) via select()/mutate(... = NULL) — downgrades plain tibble warning. Removing strata covariate column instead silently drops attribute. ❌ rowwise() supported — behaviour undefined; avoid . non-trivial pipe, confirm is_tbl_now(x) handing object diseasenowcasting.

title: tbl.now — AI Agent Skill Guide
text: autoplot() (ggplot2 generic, re-exported tbl.now) returns multi-panel patchwork diagnostic. ggplot2 hard dependency; patchwork Suggests (install ). Panels: Empirical delay distribution — case-count-weighted kernel density .delay. Observed epidemic process — get_latest_reported_cases() event_date, dashed vertical incompleteness line now - quantile(delay, level). Holidays temporal-effects spec marked red dots. Calendar effect — normalized boxplots (cases relative overall mean, 1 = average). Daily data shows day--week week--year panels; weekly shows week--year; monthly shows month--year. Seasonality periodogram — dominant peak suggests Fourier seasons length pass temporal_effects(). Key arguments: level delay quantile line drawn; default signature 1 (conservative), level = 0.95 typical choice (“dates still missing ≥5% eventual counts incomplete”).
code: library(tbl.now) autoplot(tn)                       # bare call works after library(tbl.now) autoplot(   tn,   level = 0.95,                                   # completeness threshold for the incompleteness line   delay_distribution_xlim = c(0, 10),             # per-panel x limits (all optional)   event_date_xlim = as.Date(c("2020-01-01","2020-12-31")),   calendar_effect_xlim = NULL,   seasonality_xlim = c(0, 60),   palette = .tbl_now_palette()                    # override colours )

title: Example analysis with Flusight
text: Flusight dataset (?flusight) includes weekly influenza hospital admission counts. epidemiological week (target_end_date), CDC publishes revised counts across multiple future weeks (as_of). Thus, event week associated multiple reporting dates reflecting updates revisions. Flusight dataset columns : target_end_date: epidemiological week cases occurred as_of: week CDC updated estimate event week location_name: state territory observation: reported number cases target_end_date as_of key feature dataset observation cumulative: value given target_end_date as_of latest estimate total cases event week, incremental update reporting date. following example illustrates structure: unique pair (target_end_date, as_of) therefore corresponds cumulative estimate.

title: tbl.now
text: epidemiological nowcast, typically observe two key dates: event_date: underlying event occurred (e.g., symptom onset, exposure, sample collection). report_date: event recorded data system (e.g., lab result processed, clinical visit documented). nowcasting task : estimate, past event_date, many events already occurred yet reported now. , nowcast predict many observations eventually observed event_dates. tbl.now object therefore specialized tibble() : Identifies event_date report_date columns. Stores attributes enable consistent processing. Automatically computes auxiliary fields delay, numerical indices, frequency units. Ensures dataset well-formed downstream diseasenowcasting models.

text: tbl_now() stores information structure using object attributes, ensuring consistent behavior across transformations modeling steps. primary attributes : now: “current” reporting date used nowcasting, typically recent report_date. event_date: column name storing event dates. report_date: column name storing report dates. event_units: temporal units event dates (e.g., “days”, “weeks”, “numeric”). report_units: temporal units report dates. data_type: one following (see data types section): linelist count-incidence count-cumulative. strata (optional)1: variables nowcast computed separately (e.g., age group, sex). covariates (optional): predictor variables may improve nowcast (e.g., weather covariates). is_censored (optional): identifies cases reports arrive artificial “batches” representing right-censoring rather true reporting dynamics (e.g. system error reports lab registered week ) case_count (optional): column storing case counts dataset aggregated. temporal_effects (optional): lazy specification (list temporal_effects() configs) stored via add_temporal_effects(). Columns materialised compute_temporal_effects() called. See temporal effects section details. can access attribute using corresponding getter, e.g. get_event_date() get_strata().

title: tbl.now
text: tbl_now() can represent one three data structures: Linelist: row corresponds single reported observation. Linelist data Count-incidence: row summarizes many events given event_date reported exactly report_date. Count-incidence data Count-cumulative row summarizes many events given event_date reported including report_date. distinction crucial nowcasting models operate either daily increments cumulative totals. Count-cumulative data to_count() function allows easily convert different data-types.

title: tbl.now
text: to_count() function supports structured transformations: Linelist → Count-Incidence: Aggregates event–report date, counting cases reported date. Linelist → Count-Cumulative: Aggregates event–report date, producing cumulative counts report date. Note previous example n counts 3 aggregating 1 observed report_date = 2020-09-13 2 observed report_date = 2020-09-12. difference count-incidence specifies ones observed exactly date count-cumulative specifies ones observed including date. Count-Incidence → Count-Cumulative: Computes cumulative sums event date across report dates. Aggregation within type: to_count() may also used re-aggregate datasets contain duplicate event–report pairs. useful raw surveillance feeds contain repeated entries case: dataset intentionally contains repeated event_date–report_date pairs within stratum. user wants aggregate redundant rows, to_count() function can used collapse duplicates summing case_count column. function ensures : Rows grouped event_date, report_date, strata, is_censored. case_count column summed within group. Attributes preserved resulting object remains valid tbl_now.
